label: PF Backlog 594
title: EDP: additional ObjectStore adapters (NFS/SMB, Google Drive, Azure Blob, GCS, ...) behind the ObjectStore port
body: Ports/adapters (docs/EDP-STORAGE-ADAPTERS.md): add adapters for the remaining storage backends behind the existing datastore.ObjectStore port + pass ConformObjectStore. Each backend = a new adapter (no domain changes): NFS/SMB, Google Drive, Azure Blob, GCS, and any future type. Depends on EDP-14 (S3) establishing the conformance-tested adapter pattern + EDP-16 lifecycle semantics. Capabilities declared per adapter (versioning, lock, signed URLs, multipart, CMK) so callers degrade explicitly.

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend the datastore.ObjectStore port with one adapter module per backend (NFS/SMB, Google Drive, Azure Blob, GCS), reusing the conformance harness and capability-declaration pattern established by EDP-13 (local FS) and EDP-14 (S3). No domain/port changes; each adapter declares capabilities (versioning, lock, signed URLs, multipart, CMK) and degrades explicitly when unsupported.

dependency_findings.required_state: S3 adapter + conformance pattern merged (defines adapter template)
Lifecycle semantics (versioning/lock/retention) settled for capability mapping

conflict_findings: Shares ObjectStore port and conformance harness with EDP-14/EDP-16; coordinate adapter template freeze before parallel adapter work.
Splits across adapters may contend on shared capability struct — assign one adapter per PR where possible.
duplication_findings: Local FS and S3 adapters already exist (BI-PF-1305, BI-PF-1306); do not rebuild those.
Conformance harness defined in EDP-07 (BI-PF-1299); reuse it for all new adapters.
core/*_adapters.py files are unrelated domain adapters; not candidates for reuse here.
analysis.rationale: Pure adapter expansion behind a settled port: each backend is a new, conformance-tested adapter module with declared capabilities; zero domain changes. Reuse-first by cloning the S3/local-FS adapter template and harness. Blockers are EDP-13/14/16 completion.
assumptions: EDP-13/14 adapters + conformance harness are merged and stable before this starts
Each adapter is independently shippable and optional at registration
Capability declaration mechanism from EDP-14 is reused without extension
Backends beyond the four listed (future types) follow the same adapter template
risks: Per-backend SDK/SDK-version drift and credential models vary widely
Some backends cannot support EDP-16 lifecycle features → partial capability sets
External service mocking complexity for CI conformance runs
NFS/SMB require host-level mounts; containerized CI may not provide them
evidence: BI-PF-1306 establishes conformance-tested S3 adapter pattern
BI-PF-1299 defines provider-neutral ObjectStore port + harness
BI-PF-1308 defines lifecycle semantics the capabilities must map to
missing_info: Priority order among the four backends (which first?)
Whether GCS and Google Drive are both required or Drive is lower priority/de-scoped
NFS vs SMB split: one combined adapter or two separate adapters
CI strategy for mocked external services (VCR-style vs testcontainers vs real sandbox accounts)
Credential/secret provisioning mechanism per backend for production

context_review.reason: Affected files list only docs/EDP-STORAGE-ADAPTERS.md, with no code paths/packages for new adapters; APPROACH and acceptance criteria just restate the title with no conformance-test steps, SDK/library choices, capability-flag design, or per-backend detail. Depends on unspecified EDP-14/EDP-16 patterns.
